omit.reason: Guide: "**DO NOT** apply this step with the Steam version of the game, unless you have applied the below widescreen patch! Without the modified widescreen .exe, Steam's executable copy is encrypted in such a way that executing this patcher will break it and prevent the game from launching." This plan installs on the Steam game tree without the widescreen patch (outside the Mod List).

supplemental_sections.review: Introductory heading with a warning that the general install instructions on the mod builds page must be read before starting; it contains no install action of its own. Its subsections are reviewed individually below. The manual reference run executes only the Mod List steps, in order, via manual.py on a clean vanilla Steam (Windows depot, movies removed) game tree that keeps Steam's original file name spelling, under Wine on Linux; it runs nothing from this section.

Asks the user to uninstall, delete the whole game directory and reinstall so no leftover or corrupted files or old mod data remain, then to try to clear read-only flags on the game folders. The reference run satisfies this by construction: every run starts from a freshly unpacked, verified vanilla Steam game tree, and the files in the CI working tree are writable.

Requires every archive to be fully extracted (never run TSLPatcher/HoloPatcher from inside an archive), each installer-based mod to be extracted to its own folder, the patcher to be pointed at the main game folder, loose files to go in Override with no subfolders, and warns that TSLPatcher may fail on multi-monitor setups. In the reference run each step's extract operation unpacks its archive into a fresh, separate destination under the extract root, and each patcher operation runs the mod's original TSLPatcher/HoloPatcher executable from that extracted folder under Wine, targeted at the game directory, on a single Xvfb virtual display. The linked step_ids are every Mod List step whose Installation Method line names TSLPatcher or HoloPatcher.

Warns that only one KOTOR installation may exist, because auto-detecting installers can pick the wrong one, and suggests archiving the vanilla game as a backup. The reference run has a single game tree and its patcher operations are given that game directory explicitly, so there is no second installation to be misdetected.

States that a prior build cannot be updated in place; the user must perform the zeroing step and reinstall the new build on a fresh game. The reference run always installs the current guide revision onto a fresh vanilla tree, so no prior build is present and this is satisfied.

Tells the user not to use the built-in Windows extractor and to use WinRAR or 7-Zip instead, because the native extractor fails on many of these archives. Not applicable to the reference run, which runs on Linux and extracts archives with manual.py's extract operation (7z for RAR/7z archives, Python zip/tar support otherwise) into fresh destinations.

Platform note for AMD graphics cards: random in-game crashes are fixed by updating drivers, or by rolling back to the linked older driver series. This is a runtime/driver environment note that does not change game files; it is not applicable to the reference run, which installs mods and does not play the game.
Points Mac OS players to a separate page for installing the game and these mods. Not applicable: the reference run uses the Windows Steam depot under Wine on Linux, not the Mac OS version.

States that the Amazon Games release ships a modified executable and .ini that break the Miles sound system and disable movies and sound, and links a fix to apply. Not applicable: the reference run uses the Steam Windows depot, not the Amazon Games release, so this fix is not applied.

Warns that case-sensitive Linux file systems require batch-lowercasing mod files before installer-based mods and again across the game directory afterwards, and notes Proton crash/rendering issues. The CI environment handles the case issue without lowercasing anything: manual.py matches every copy, rename and delete path against existing game entries case-insensitively (PyKotor CaseAwarePath), so a copied file overwrites an existing entry that differs only in case under its existing name instead of creating a duplicate, as on Windows, and the original patchers run under Wine, which looks up file names case-insensitively; Proton gameplay issues are not applicable because the run installs under Wine and does not play the game.

Informational: describes a rare load-screen crash from a data overflow, worked around by temporarily disabling 'Frame Buffer Effects' and 'Soft Shadows' in the advanced graphics options. This is an in-game settings workaround, not an install step, and names no mod; the reference run makes no change for it.

Informational: about 7GB of mod archives excluding movies, about 14GB installed including base game files excluding upscaled movies, and about 25GB with Pops Maellard's HD movies at 1920x1080. No install action; the reference run does not use it.
Introduces an optional tool that speeds up TSLPatcher installs, noting no true mod manager exists for KOTOR. It is optional and not part of the reference install; the run does not use it.

Optional registry-edit script that creates desktop symlinks to the KOTOR and KOTOR 2 directories so TSLPatcher's folder picker is quicker to use; the guide notes it does not work on Mac (or likely Linux) and changes no game files. It is optional and NOT used by this reference: patcher operations are invoked with the game directory explicitly under Wine, so no folder picker shortcut is needed.

supplemental_sections.source_heading: ## Optional Widescreen & Extended Widescreen Support Mods
supplemental_sections.review: Optional section: recommends applying the UniWS widescreen patch from the linked video (which edits the executable and means the game must then be launched directly rather than through Steam), then the widescreen mods listed below. This reference does NOT apply UniWS or any mod in this section; the reference install is the Mod List only, at the vanilla executable's resolution support.

Optional loose-file bugfix by MadDerp that fixes turret cockpit visuals exposed by widescreen. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional .bat patcher with loose-file components by ndix UR that edits swkotor.exe (after UniWS) so in-game menus render at the widescreen resolution, then places the HR Menus files for the chosen resolution in Override. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional loose-file patch by ndix UR with rebuilt high-resolution menu UI elements, described as a mandatory patch for 'HR Menus'. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional loose-file camera tweak by Darth Parametric for the Workbench upgrade screen at higher resolutions. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional loose-file upscale of the game's icons by ajdrenter, recommended with 'HR Menus'; the guide recommends the .tpc option and not overwriting when prompted for this mod only. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

supplemental_sections.source_heading: ### Robe Icons for JC's Cloaked Robes
supplemental_sections.review: Optional loose-file mod 'HD Robe Icons for JC's Cloaked Jedi Robes' by Nehua, whose master is 'JC's Cloaked Jedi Robes'; the user copies the icons matching the robe version installed in that Mod List step. The linked step is the Mod List step '### Cloaked Jedi Robes'. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional loose-file HD computer interface by Dark Hope, mainly useful in widescreen. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional loose-file fix by Doiinko for uneven screen fades at modded resolutions. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional loose-file fix by DarthParametric that widens the main menu view for widescreen. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install.

Optional movie replacement 'K1 Cutscenes Rescaled' by Pops Maellard (about 15GB); its files go in the movies folder, with resolution and 30fps choices made at download. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install. The run's game tree also has its movies removed, and no movie files are installed.

Optional alternative movie replacement 'KOTOR Remastered Cutscenes' by naelavok, to be used instead of Pops Maellard's set; files go in the movies folder, and the guide notes the title crawl movie will not play with it. This reference does not install it: the optional/widescreen mods are outside the Mod List and are not part of the reference install. The run's game tree also has its movies removed, and no movie files are installed.
Introductory heading for troubleshooting notes on base-game problems that are not caused by the build. The subsections are runtime workarounds reviewed below; the reference run applies none of them.

Informational: a base-game crash after character creation (or on later load screens) is avoided by disabling 'Frame Buffer Effects' in the in-game Advanced Graphics Options. This is an in-game setting, not an install step or a game file change made by this reference; the run does not play the game and makes no change for it.

Informational: an engine bug where the character is stuck after combat, tied to the framerate not syncing with the monitor refresh rate; the fix is v-sync and/or setting the monitor to 60Hz, and checking for interfering software. These are display/system settings, not game file changes; the reference run does not apply anything for them.

Optional, untested workaround: a linked Steam discussion fix for grass rendering issues (reported to make many textures partially transparent), or disabling grass in the .ini, which the guide recommends. Either option would change user configuration rather than install a mod; this reference does not apply either and leaves the vanilla .ini as shipped.

Informational: if the swoop bike floats above the track, temporarily launch the game in Windows XP SP3 compatibility mode for the race, then turn it off. This is a launch-time compatibility setting, not a game file change; it is not applicable to the reference run, which does not launch or play the game.
